subject: Meteorology
title: Fogbows and Cloudbows
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fogbows and Cloudbows.

hook.text: Fogbows are rainbows made by tiny fog droplets—they appear as ghostly white arcs instead of colorful bands.

buildup.text: Fog droplets are so small (under 0.05 mm) that diffraction dominates over refraction—smearing the colors together.

discovery.text: The result is a broad white band with faint reddish outer and bluish inner edges—a rainbow drained of its color.

twist.text: Cloudbows seen from aircraft are similar—and can form complete circles with the aircraft's shadow at the center.

climax.text: Moonbows (lunar rainbows) also exist—so faint that they appear white to the eye, but cameras reveal their colors.

punchline.text: A rainbow without color—proof that droplet size matters.

quiz.question: Why do fogbows appear white instead of colorful?
options: Tiny droplets cause diffraction that smears colors together
